title: k-means with k-means++ initialization
hints: Squared distances from every point to every centroid in one shot: ((X[:, None, :] - C[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(-1) has shape (N, k); labels are its argmin over axis 1.

k-means++: pick the first centroid uniformly, then repeatedly pick a data point with probability proportional to its squared distance to the nearest centroid chosen so far (rng.choice(N, p=d2 / d2.sum())). Keep d2 as the running minimum.

Lloyd's loop: assign, record the inertia, move each centroid to the mean of its points (keep the old centroid if a cluster is empty), stop when the centroids move less than tol. Each of the two steps can only lower the objective, which is why the history never goes up.
